summary:
Per-bank counts: Goldman 2, Apollo/Slok 1 (3 items, 2 banks/strategists).

Goldman research (via MikeZaccardi) covers macro data: a Core Retail Sales beat lifting the Q3 GDP tracking estimate to +3.0%, alongside a decomposition of the labor share decline into pass-through entities, depreciation, and equity comp rather than a pure labor-to-capital shift.

Torsten Slok (Apollo) argues hyperscaler CDS widening reflects a repricing of deteriorating credit fundamentals — debt-financed AI capex, rising leverage, negative FCF — rather than dealer hedging.

No @neilksethi/@neilksethinew tweets appeared in this collection window. All 3 items were sourced via relay account MikeZaccardi; no cross-account duplicates found. The remaining 57 considered tweets were dropped as untagged chart/meme content (mostly MikeZaccardi, TheChartReport) without a matched bank/strategist tag.

items.author: MikeZaccardi
items.text:
GS: 40% of the labor share decline isn't a shift from labor to capital 📉📊

It's:
1️⃣ Pass-through entities: Tax incentives moved wage income into business profits 🏢
2️⃣ Depreciation: More tech/software means faster capital wear-and-tear 💻
3️⃣ Equity comp 📈 https://t.co/cxBHxvn2D0

banks.theme: Torsten Slok: hyperscaler CDS widening reflects AI-capex credit repricing, not dealer hedging

items.author: MikeZaccardi
items.text:
Hyperscaler CDS widening isn't dealer hedging... otherwise, bank spreads would be moving too 📉. 

Instead, the market is repricing deteriorating credit fundamentals: debt-financed AI capex, rising leverage, and negative FCF with uncertain ROI 🤖💸.

Torsten at Apollo https://t.co/20qAPzC8Re
